American Airlines is focused on operating as many remaining flights as possible this evening while positioning the airline for the strongest possible recovery tomorrow and in the days ahead.

For the remainder of the evening, we are prioritizing flights to non-hub cities, as well as international flying, to position aircraft and crew where they are needed to help restore our operation. We expect residual delays and cancellations tonight and into tomorrow following the FAA’s nationwide ground stop.

JetBlue cancelled all of its remaining domestic flights on Friday. Frontier says “we are working to restore operations.” Southwest says flights have resumed, but “customers may continue to experience delays and cancellations as we work to recover our operation.”
A mess of a press conference
Did they admit fault or not?

Duffy and Mullin went out of their way to blame the antiquated ATC infrastructure, and even more out of their way to blame Congress and everyone that came before them for not funding a complete replacement of the system. But they also seemed to say that the network upgrades made by Duffy’s FAA also played some role in the crash. “What it appears to be right now is, as Secretary Duffy and FAA was going in and putting patches into the system, they were putting new equipment and new technology, and that new equipment, new technology…it was overwhelming the older system,” Mullin said. Duffy also said that routers were “overloaded with data.”
There weren’t many specifics and it wasn’t very clear exactly what went wrong.
This was Chris Cameron’s takeaway at the New York Times:

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy appeared to suggest that his effort to upgrade air traffic control infrastructure may have contributed to the outage, but he defended the upgrades by arguing that it had to be done.
“By doing nothing, you inject way more risk into the system,” he said, adding, “I didn’t anticipate that we would have an outage like this.”
It also wasn’t clear whether the contractor L3Harris was at all involved.
New patches overwhelmed the old system, or something
We’re obviously might need to wait for a more technical explanation from better public speakers regarding what actually happened.
And this was after practically no new information from the FAA or the Trump administration for hours.
A ‘legacy network problem’
It’s not my or Trump’s fault
That was the basic point of most of what Duffy said.
This was Duffy’s explanation
And most of it was blaming others, with some small amounts of useful information mixed in about this actual crisis:
And it wasn’t until almost ten minutes into the press conference when Duffy finally sounded like a public servant:
Next time maybe open with that instead of the DHS secretary joking about how it’s Friday the 13th and then complaining about stuff he read on the internet.
‘It doesn’t appear’ that a cyberattack or rogue AI were behind the outage
Mullin says they are investigating, and “there’s nothing completely certain right now.”
This was Mullin’s actual announcement related to the ground stop
Duffy is praising Trump and asking for money
He says today’s outage is why he should get the $50 billion in emergency funding he wants to build a new state-of-the-art air traffic control system. And he has praised Trump at least a dozen times.
Mullin and Duffy are giving a briefing
Mullin is again acting kind of weird. He didn’t announce anything about the ground stop at all. He seemed most interested in explaining how the conspiracy theories about the outage were not true.
The ground stop has been lifted
We’re still waiting for the White House briefing to start.
Jetblue cancels all domestic flights tonight
If you’re not in line, stay at home
You may remember L3Harris from such previous Trump administration deals as …
The Wall Street Journal and CBS News report that L3Harris is the contractor who manages the system which appears to have crashed today.

The company is the defense contractor who got the contract to retrofit the luxury Boeing 747 that Qatar gave President Trump and make it the new Air Force One (which Trump will probably try to keep when he leaves office).
It also got a billion dollar investment, in the form of a convertible preferred security, from the Pentagon in January for its Missile Solutions spinoff company that produces solid rocket motors.
For the Airplane! uninitiated, that’s this scene:
It appears some international departures are resuming, but not domestic
This right now may just be a software glitch, but …
From James Fallows’s New York Times Magazine story about whether or not air travel is now less safe under the Trump administration:

Over the past 22 months, the rate of airplane accidents and close calls has suggested a system under enormous strain. Here is an incomplete list of the incidents we’ve seen in the months since the Jan. 29, 2025, Potomac crash:

March 5, 2025: Debris from a failed SpaceX rocket launch affects civilian airliners. Nov. 24, 2025, Louisville, Ky.: An engine rips away from a UPS cargo jet on takeoff, killing all three members of the flight crew and 12 people on the ground. Dec. 12, 2025: A JetBlue flight diverts to avoid a military tanker that had turned off its transponder as part of an operation in the Caribbean, the first of several such episodes. Feb. 27, 2026, San Antonio: A police helicopter crosses the path of a plane cleared for landing. March 2, 2026, Burbank, Calif.: A TV news helicopter wanders into the path of another landing plane. March 22, 2026, New York: An Air Canada jet strikes a fire truck that was cleared to cross its path at LaGuardia Airport, killing the two Air Canada pilots. May 17, 2026, Idaho: Two Navy EA-18G Growler electronic-warfare planes collide during the “Gunfighter Skies” air show. July 15, 2026, Pensacola, Fla.: A Navy Blue Angels demo flight comes dangerously close to civilian spectators. Aug. 4, 2026, Washington: Marine One takes off toward the path of a departing regional jet. Sept. 6, 2026, Miami International Airport: A cargo jet subcontracting to Amazon overshoots a runway on landing and kills five airport employees in an airport van.

This is an extraordinary series of lapses, by any measure. Many of these could have been mass-casualty events, and three did involve fatalities. The Marine One incident was alarming for a different reason. The two aircraft didn’t come close enough to put them in real danger, but the helicopter was carrying President Trump — and, as the N.T.S.B. later found, its crew had taken off from the White House Ellipse before National Airport’s control tower received its required three-minute departure call. (The White House, the Department of Transportation and the Pentagon declined to provide specific answers to questions I sent them.)
All of this appears to be at odds with the cardinal principles that have made modern U.S. aviation so safe.
Overheard on a rerouted flight
Overheard at an airport: ‘We do not listen to robots’
And there is conflicting reporting!
Some pilots say they needed to use the emergency frequency
The FAA has asked multiple countries to halt their air traffic to the U.S.
Only the mainland U.S. was affected
The ground stop did not apply to regional flights in Hawaii and Alaska, according to Alaska Airlines:

Flights within the state of Alaska and Neighbor Island flights in Hawai’i are not impacted. Flights from the West Coast to Hawai’i can continue, and international flights from Honolulu have also been cleared for departure. Aircraft in the air are continuing to their destinations.
It may have been a software update
CBS News’ Olivia Rinaldi reports:
Multiple sources tell @CBSNews that an update to the private communications network that connects America’s air traffic control system caused the system to reboot.
When the FAA’s telecommunication infrastructure rebooted, it crashed, causing the communications outage.
The system is operated by L3Harris.
Now that are more than 2,400 flight cancellations and counting.
The sports world is probably gonna feel this too
Though the full extent of the impact is not yet clear. The Athletic has a liveblog devoted just to this topic, here’s what David Ubben wondered about college football teams:

I’m curious about the prospect of teams flying to games on the same day they’re supposed to be be played. A lot of these games have high stakes and a lot of potential money involved. And coaches are creatures of habit who have their own livelihoods at stake. I would expect schools to buck hard at any suggestion they could travel early tomorrow morning and kick off at night.
Utah and Tennessee say no discussions about contingency plans yet. They’re just waiting for word from the FAA and in the process of eating dinner.
The National Weather Service says it’s fine
Duckworth is demanding answers
We’d like some too, but she’s the ranking Democrat on the Senate’s Aviation, Space, and Innovation subcommittee:
The affected telecom network may be managed by a single company
The Wall Street Journal reports:

The outage appears to be affecting a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to people briefed on the matter. The network handles crucial radio frequencies that air-traffic controllers use to communicate with pilots, the people said. It wasn’t immediately clear whether the outage also affected the radar feeds that controllers use to keep aircraft safely separated in the skies.
An L3Harris spokeswoman didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
1,700 cancellations and counting
Stuck streaming on the tarmac at LAX
Our colleague Devon Ivie says she was just stuck on the tarmac for 90 minutes in Los Angeles, but she was able to watch Minions and Monsters to pass the time.
The communication problems appear to have started in Chicago
Air Current reports that the problems originated at the Chicago ARTCC and spread quickly to other facilities:

The FAA’s Washington, D.C. command center was notified around 3:30 pm local time that multiple air centers around the country had lost communication, radio frequencies and radar, TAC has learned. The outages began with the Chicago air traffic route control center, with Boston, Washington, New York and Minneapolis verifying they had problems as well in rapid succession.

At that point the FAA decided to issue a ground stop for all aircraft flying to the east of the national air system. As that call was being made, more air traffic facilities began experiencing communications and frequency malfunctions and U.S. authorities extended the ground stop nationwide.
So about that SMART AI system the FAA just added

In September, the FAA announced the limited rollout of a $875 million software package called SMART, for “Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories,” that is aimed at “fundamentally reshaping how we manage our airspace.” Initially, only flights in Washington, D.C. area were affected. Built by the Boston-based data company Air Space Intelligence (ASI), the new system use AI to process hundreds of data inputs and automatically plan aircraft routes. In one segment that aired on CNN, the system was shown routing a flight over a line of thunderstorms, instead of around them, saving 42 minutes of flight time.

On October 13, 23 Democratic members of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure sent a letter to the Government Accountability Office asking it to review the system, given that that it could “hallucinate safety-critical information.” The lawmakers stated that “the use of artificial intelligence within SMART has rightfully raised serious questions about its reliability and safety benefits.”

Despite such concerns, the FAA decided to move forward to a full rollout. Three days ago, on November 10, the FAA released a statement saying that “After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public.”
It is these Air Traffic Command Centers (ARTCC) that have been hit by today’s outage.
ASI says its system is not involved in the outage:
The skies are getting a lot less crowded
Apparently SpaceX rocket flights aren’t grounded
President Trump is posting about a congressional bill centered on the entertainment industry. At least people stuck in airports and airplanes will have something long to read:
Stuck on the tarmac in Chicago
The New York Times passes along one passenger’s experience from inside a grounded plane at O’Hare:

“I have no idea when or if they’re going to allow departures for today,” a United pilot told a flight bound for Rochester, N.Y., that sat on the tarmac for 45 minutes waiting to take off from Chicago O’Hare International Airport.
After an hour, the pilot tried to turn back to the terminal, telling passengers, “We’re definitely going back to the gate.”
But not even that was possible. There was so much congestion and confusion at the airport as planes jockeyed for gate space, some flights on the tarmac had nowhere to go.
“We were so close to getting out,” said Barbara Bullock, who was heading from Colorado to upstate New York on a college tour with her 17-year-old daughter. But not anymore. “Friday the 13th.”
The airlines are expecting this to last ‘for the rest of day’
In a statement, American Airlines indicated that it’s anticipating disruptions to its flights to continue throughout Friday.

“Flights already in the air can continue to their destinations. We expect disruption to our schedule for the rest of the day, depending on the length of the FAA’s nationwide ground stop. It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop,” the statement read.
‘This is absolutely unbelievable that this could happen in this day and age’
Explained an aviation expert to CBS News:

“This is absolutely unprecendented,” said Robert Sumwalt, a former chair of the National Transportation Safety Board and a CBS News transportation safety expert. “I was an airline pilot for 24 years. I was in the air at on 9/11. That was the last major ground stop. There was one back in 2023 for just a few hours. This is absolutely unbelievable that this could happen in this day and age.”
Thousands and thousands of flights impacted
According to FlightAware, there are now 1,195 cancellations and 9,917 delays for flights into and out of the U.S. today, as of 5:41 p.m. ET.

There were more than 4,000 airborne flights in the U.S. at the time when the ground stop was ordered. Again, they are all being allowed to land, and there is no indication that any of those passengers are in danger. Just after 5 p.m. the FAA announced that all inbound flights would be handled on a case by case basis.
More than a million passengers may be affected tonight
The aviation data and analytics company Cirium estimates upwards of 1.5 million passengers are scheduled to fly today from 4 p.m. ET onwards in the U.S.
This is going to be a while

Just heard over at ATC.com: a controller at North Las Vegas ground control tower told a private aircraft that “it’s going to be at least 8 hours for the indefinite ground stop, but no information besides that.”
Per the New York Times, passengers at multiple airports have already been told to go home if they live nearby.

Notably, Mullin kept referencing the most high-profile instance of the FAA ordering a complete ground stop — September 11, 2001 — hoping to reassure Americans that today’s stoppage was nothing like the aftermath of the nation’s deadliest terrorist attack.
“This isn’t another 9/11,” he said. “This is a communications outage.”
Never stop being you, Trump administration
Mullin says “no indication” that this was a nefarious attack

In a hastily-assembled press conference, Homeland Security Secretary Mullin tried to ease the public’s concerns about the cause of the ground stop. “There was no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack. It is just a telecommunication outage as of right now,” he said.

The secretary continued, “Everybody’s safe. There’s no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they’re flying or anything like that,” he said. “I just want to make sure everybody is at ease about that.”

U.S. national airspace shut down unexpectedly shortly afer 3:30 p.m. this afternoon, as aircraft waiting to take off at airports across the country were informed that the FAA had put in place a “national ground stop.” The shutdown hit air travel during one of the busiest times of the week, as business travelers return home from work trips and vacationers head out to their destinations. Inbound aircraft continued to land normally.

Over the air-traffic-control app ATC.com, controllers could be heard informing flight crew that they had received a message stating “all aircraft, all airports ground stopped until 22Z (5 p.m. EST) due to a nationwide equipment outage.”

At the site LiveATC.net, an American pilot could be heard saying that the company had told its aircraft to return to their gates, implying that they expect the delay to be prolonged. Other aircraft continued to line up on taxiways for eventual clearance to take off.

The outage apparently affected Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which handle aircraft during the cruise phase in between airports, but there was no indication of what might be causing the problem, and at time of writing it wasn’t clear if planes in this phase of flight were having trouble getting or receiving transmissions over the radio.

CNN reports that two law-enforcement officials said a cyberattack was unlikely to have caused the outage. There has also been speculation that a new AI system integrated into the FAA might be responsible, but that system, called SMART, is used for planning and scheduling, not for communication with aircraft.

Since the start of the second Trump administration, officials have come under increasing criticism for a raft of system failures and safety violations. On Thursday, the New York Times published a long feature by James Fallows titled, “Is Air Travel Less Safe?” which asserts that “Over the past 22 months, the rate of airplane accidents and close calls has suggested a system under enormous strain.”

items.title: Van Hollen Challenge to Schumer Raises Odds of Government Shutdown
items.description: Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen has decided to fight Chuck Schumer for the position of Senate Majority Leader in the 120th Congress. The conflict is ostensibly about choosing the best strategist and tactician for the 55 or 56 Democrats who will spend the nex
items.author: Ed Kilgore
paragraphs: Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen has decided to fight Chuck Schumer for the position of Senate Majority Leader in the 120th Congress. The conflict is ostensibly about choosing the best strategist and tactician for the 55 or 56 Democrats who will spend the next two years constraining the Trump administration and paving the way (they hope) for a 2029 Democratic trifecta regime. But it’s also going to have more immediate implications for congressional Democrats.

Van Hollen’s leadership bid seems partly ideological (he is the putative champion of Senate progressives despite his own mainstream background) and partly pitched to appeal to a widespread desire for novelty in light of Democrats’ massive midterm gains.

The 75-year-old Schumer has been in his position for a decade (as of January) and is generally considered a poor (and decidedly un-hip) developer and purveyor of the party message. Still, it’s more than a bit unusual to dump a leader immediately after so successful an election cycle, which is why Van Hollen’s challenge came as a surprise. He’s claiming “double-digit” support among old and new senators; so far only Bernie Sanders and senators-elect Abdul El-Sayed and Peggy Flanagan have publicly endorsed him, whereas Schumer has a growing list of loyalists backing his candidacy. Skeptical that he has any chance of success, most observers believe Van Hollen is seeking leverage for younger and more progressive Democrats. In that respect, the leadership fight will inevitably become conflated with a long-awaited “struggle for the soul of the Democratic Party” which will include a wide-open 2028 presidential competition.

Indeed, it’s very likely that the leadership battle (which will be resolved by a secret ballot among Senate Democrats at some point in early December) will be the opening act of the 2028 Democratic passion play for one simple reason: It will coincide with a December 11 congressional deadline for dealing with the expiration of a stopgap spending measure enacted in September to defer major budgetary decisions until after the midterm elections.

Normally you’d expect Democrats to kick the can down the road with another stopgap measure that would defer the real spending decisions until they are firmly in control of Congress after January, and there’s some reporting that Schumer and his Senate allies are inclined in that direction. But Van Hollen (joined by Sanders, Tammy Duckworth, and Michael Bennet) has already announced his opposition to any short-term spending deal that doesn’t include a cutoff of funds for continuation of the Iran War.

This blunt advocacy of a government shutdown just prior to Christmas (given the very low odds of Donald Trump agreeing to acceptable language on Iran) in conjunction with the leadership election will put enormous pressure on Schumer to take the same position. After all, Schumer’s current unsavory reputation among progressives and other Democratic activists dates back to his abrupt March 2025 decision to abandon a threat to shut down the federal government in the face of massive provocations from Trump, Elon Musk’s DOGE initiative, and power grabs by OMB Director Russell Vought. Another “surrender” by Schumer, even if it’s a temporary maneuver to get Democrats into a position of greater control over spending decisions, could give enormous impetus to Van Hollen’s challenge.

Right now restive progressives and other self-styled representatives of the Democratic “base” are spoiling for fights both with Trump and with establishment Democrats, and efforts to stop the Iran War are the most obvious flash-point. So unless Schumer can craft some sort of accommodation with his intraparty critics that heads off Van Hollen’s challenge, all hell could break out right away. Federal employees and contractors facing a hungry holiday season could become collateral damage in the first big post-election fight, even before its winners take office.

items.title: City Leaders Press Google Over AI Schools Plan
items.description: City leaders are demanding answers from Google after the company recently suggested that school districts’ restrictions on artificial intelligence could result in students being unable to use Google Search. City Council Speaker Julie Menin and Shekar Krishnan,
items.author: Nia Prater
paragraphs: City leaders are demanding answers from Google after the company recently suggested that school districts’ restrictions on artificial intelligence could result in students being unable to use Google Search. City Council Speaker Julie Menin and Shekar Krishnan, the chair of the Council’s Committee on Oversight and Investigation, issued a joint letter to Google’s CEO Sundar Pichai, requesting more information on the tech giant’s planned AI restrictions on the school level and what they might mean for students and educators.

“No private company should have an outsized influence on the way our children are educated. Rather than giving more choice to our educators, as the company claims, this decision would force schools to embrace AI products in order to maintain access to the most widely used online search tool. The Council won’t sit idly by while decisions about our children’s education are effectively shifted from educators to the leaders of for-profit companies,” Menin and Krishnan said in a statement.

Last week, Google detailed new restrictions on its artificial-intelligence learning tools, revealing it will automatically turn off student access to its Gemini products as well as Google Search unless school administrators actively opt into those services. The company followed up with a social-media post, saying that schools can choose to turn off Gemini, Gemini Notebook, or Search individually, or any combination of the three. “We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control. That’s exactly why we are making these changes today to address the feedback we’ve heard from educators in recent months. And we’ll continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure we are giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved Search for learning,” the post read.

But a subsequent comment from a top leader at the company has prompted concerns among parents and educators alike that the restrictions could go even further in some school districts that have implemented stricter regulations around AI use. In an interview with the New York Times last week, Google’s vice-president for education, Chris Philips, described search and AI as being “deeply integrated.” He added that if AI use was banned at a school that students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

The remark, coupled with the company’s overall announcement, prompted swift backlash. Protesters gathered outside Google offices in Chicago and New York City this week, demonstrating against what they see as the slow creep of AI use into the classroom.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose administration rolled out a one-year moratorium on generative-AI use in the city’s public schools, suggested Google’s policy essentially pressures schools into embracing AI or risk losing access to key educational tools. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools. No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children. Our public schools exist to serve students, not to grow the profit margins of Big Tech,” he wrote Tuesday on X.

In their joint letter, Menin and Krishnan noted how deeply interwoven the use of Google products is into city school life, including the daily use of programs like Google Classroom, Google docs, and Google Search, as well as the use of Chromebooks. Among the questions they want answered are whether Google will allow city public-school students to use Search without having to opt into AI tools, and what safeguards, if any, the company has implemented to ensure schools have a choice when it comes to AI adoption, as well as queries on the accuracy of Gemini’s information and data collection.

“New York City Public Schools has made deliberate decisions about how technology should support classroom learning and protect students. Google must continue to respect those decisions, especially given New Yorkers’ substantial taxpayer investment in its products and services. Having secured a dominant presence in our schools, Google should not use that position to pressure districts into adopting AI tools they do not want for their students,” Menin and Krishnan wrote.

items.title: Tyra Banks Leapt Out of a Car to Help an Aspiring Model
items.description: Looks like Rihanna's little lookalike isn't the only aspiring model getting a little boost from supermodel and business mogul Tyra Banks.
items.author: Sandra Song
paragraphs: Looks like Rihanna's little lookalike isn't the only aspiring model getting a little boost from supermodel and business mogul Tyra Banks.
Over the weekend, Banks was at BeautyCon LA when she spotted beauty YouTuber Tatyana Ali in the middle of a curbside photo shoot. So, naturally, she leapt out of her car to assist.

Retelling the story via her Instagram earlier today, Banks shared her favorite shot of Ali, writing, "When you go to @beautycon and you're in your car leaving but you see a photo shoot happening that is kind of going in the wrong direction."

"What else do you do but put on your Super/Model/Hero cape, jump out of the car, grab the camera from the photographer and start clicking," Banks continued, before adding, "Maybe one day I'll jump out of the car to capture YOU. #TyraTaughtMe."
That said, Banks was quick to also acknowledge that the photographer eventually "took some amazing photos" after a quick five-minute lesson.

Not only that, but Ali also ended up posting a photo of Banks behind the camera, writing, "Soo today THEEE TYRA BANKS got out of her car to take photos of me. BASICALLY this is most iconic moment in my life." Ali then went on to joke, "Quick question though Tyra, can you just sign me?"
Check out her post, below.

items.title: Did Madonna Invent the Pop Star Remix Album?
items.description: After four months of nothing but Brat, Charli xcx decided it was time for more Brat.
items.author: Joan Summers
paragraphs: After four months of nothing but Brat, Charli xcx decided it was time for more Brat.

Specifically, the completely remixed version of the original LP (Brat and it’s completely different but also still brat), which flexed features from Bb trickz, Julian Casablancas, Ariana Grande, to reimagine the entire Brat tracklist. The result was pretty much a second Brat that also wasn’t Brat at all. The title didn’t lie.

Since then, it feels like every main pop girl has opted for a remix album instead of tacking a few new tracks onto a deluxe. Brat and its completely different broke through a ceiling in the slightly left-of-center pop mainstream, as if she reminded us and her contemporaries that full remix albums were even an option. We’ve since seen similar efforts from Rose Gray, PinkPantheress, and Smerz, and more are on the way, like Zara Larsson’s upcoming Girl’s Trip.
But by no means did Charli create the remix album.

Like most things pop culture, all remix album roads lead back to the Mothers: Madonna and Janet. On You Can Dance (1987), Madonna reimagined tracks from her first three albums, while janet. Remixed (1995) only features about half of the original janet. tracklist. Jennifer Lopez and Britney Spears would usher the trend into the 2000s with J to tha L-O! and the first volume of B in the Mix. Mariah Carey would similarly release the club classic The Remixes in 2003. But by the late 2000s, the remix album had largely given way to the bonus-track deluxe, especially as “mainstream” pop moved away from those gritty club tracks that could be more intuitively remixed. Think: Adele, Bruno Mars, Mumford & Sons.

Among all the big-name pop stars throughout the 2010s, like One Direction, Ariana Grande (My Everything), and especially Taylor Swift, deluxe editions would become defining parts of their catalogues. And the bonus-track deluxe is still kicking: Sabrina Carpenter’s Short n Sweet (Deluxe) and Olivia Rodrigo’s GUTS (spilled) are perfectly recent examples of what feels like the industry-standard deluxe form. Charli herself did it with Crash just two years before Brat, adding four new songs to the original tracklist while actively playing the Main Pop Girl game.

Even as mainstream pop battled between EDM and “ho-hey!” in the 2010s, remix albums persisted in the underground electronic and R&B spaces. Kelela has released top-to-bottom remix projects since the Cut 4 Me EP and her debut album Hallucinogen in 2015, getting renditions from artists like Kaytranada, Princess Nokia, and Yaeji. Kaytranada, specifically, has become a kind of cosigner in that pop-R&B-club space, with his remixes serving as a go-to bridge between scenes (Rochelle Jordan, Kali Uchis), ushering that ever-changing sonic spirit into the 2020s.

Into the late 2010s, pop remixes were mostly one-offs: Calvin Harris’ Funk Wav remix of SZA’s “The Weekend,” Lorde compiling the very-of-the-time group of Post Malone, SZA, and Khalid for a 2018-pilled “Homemade Dynamite.” Early in the Brat rollout, when we’d only heard the “Von dutch” remix with Addison Rae and A.G. Cook, this seemed the more likely route for Charli.

In the pandemic era, as pop turned back toward the dancefloor and artists had more time to experiment, Dua Lipa and Lady Gaga both released their own ravey dance-pop LPs (Future Nostalgia and Chromatica, respectively), each with a remixed counterpart. Dua went on to drop Club Future Nostalgia, a collab with The Blessed Madonna that evokes ‘90s British radio-DJ mixes, featuring remixes by Jayda G, Mark Ronson, and London disco mainstays Horse Meat Disco. Gaga recruited a grab-bag of hyperpop, triphop, and electronic artists for Dawn of Chromatica, with remixes and occasional verses from Ashnikko, Arca, Shygirl and Dorian Electra. Dawn, specifically, follows the same tracklist order as Chromatica, making it feel even more like an evil counterpart.

When Tame Impala’s Rushium tour was put on pause at the start of the pandemic, just weeks after he dropped his fourth full-length, The Slow Rush, Kevin Parker released The Slow Rush in an Imaginary Place. It’s less of an on-the-nose remix album than an environmental reinterpretation, with ambient crowd chatter and a faraway effect that sounds like the album is reverberating from the club across the street. This was also a less formal “drop” (released to SoundCloud and YouTube rather than an official streaming release), but it’s a reinterpretation that gets at the sonic malleability at the core of remix efforts, especially in the electro-pop space. And in that same vein, on the production side, Parker’s work with Dua Lipa on 2024’s Radical Optimism resulted in an extended cut of the LP that added 20 minutes of music to the original tracklist, offering a trancey counterpart to the original’s pure pop sensibilities.

This is to say that Charli xcx didn’t so much invent the remix album as she did reintroduce it to the masses. If anything, Charli’s roots in remix albums, specifically, lie with A.G. Cook’s PC Music label/collective, which gave rise to artists like Danny L Harle, SOPHIE, and EasyFun, who then utilized that ethos with artists outside the scene.
Brat and it’s completely different but also still Brat feels like the inflection point, where remix LPs were officially “back” for the mainstream listener.

The drop coincided with her midweek midday livestream listening party at an upstate New York art installation, Charli teasing songs in a similarly frenetic, Boiler Room-type energy. Some of her biggest features (Lorde, Billie Eilish, Troye Sivan) rolled out as a slow drip, holding us over for the summer. And those songs, with their underlying gossip and subsequently internet-combusting lyrics — Lorde’s “Girl, so confusing” verse, Eilish’s “Charli likes boys, but she knows I’d hit it” on “Guess” — landed as “moments” in their own right.

Part of what made Brat and it’s completely different feel so expansive in the mainstream was the way she thoroughly reworked most of the original material. Tracks became completely new compositions, with new elements and melody lines that changed the song’s original tone (see: “Talk talk featuring troye sivan” only building off the original’s bridge, or the “Owner of a Broken Heart” sample added to “Mean girls featuring julian casablancas”).

Since then, Rose Gray released A Little Louder, Please in October, the remix-deluxe (featuring JADE with remixes from Logic1000 and Alex Chapman) that built on the slow-burning hype the original fostered throughout the year. PinkPantheress more than quadrupled the Fancy That runtime with her three-disc behemoth, Fancy Some More?, which split the tracklist into a slew of features that leaned into each artist’s style and a separate set of remixes that showcased her UK underground inspirations. As if to say, “Yes, I’m giving you three versions of ‘Illegal’ and four versions of ‘Stateside,’ and you’re gonna listen to all of them!”

At the top of the year, Lily Allen teased a West End Girl remix LP in Interview at the top of the year, while Zara Larsson (who cited Charli as inspiration) confirmed a Midnight Sun remix album is imminent. Is everyone just playing catch-up? It feels like something of an expectation now: every pop album that makes a splash must reignite the conversation with a complete reinterpretation. Brat and it’s completely different still held the surprise and spectacle, but each one since then, regardless of how good some of the songs are, comes across as a box-checking obligation.
It also begs the question of when a remix album is and isn’t necessary.

Would the dancefloor underwhelm of Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally benefit from a more balls-to-the-walls trance-house makeover? To me, yes. But is something like a Sabrina Carpenter feature on Lily Allen's "Tennis" going to hit the same as Pink and Zara's “Stateside”? Probably not. If everything is stage-setting for reinvention, then reinvention stops meaning anything at all.

items.title: Zendaya “Felt Overwhelmed” on the Set of ‘The Odyssey.’ Luckily, Tom Holland Came to Support Her
items.description: On the set of The Odyssey, in which Zendaya plays the goddess Athena, there were some particularly challenging days, as the actor recalled during a recent special screening attended by the cast at Los Angeles’s Academy Museum of Motion Pictures. While filming
items.author: Alessandra De Tommasi
paragraphs: On the set of The Odyssey, in which Zendaya plays the goddess Athena, there were some particularly challenging days, as the actor recalled during a recent special screening attended by the cast at Los Angeles’s Academy Museum of Motion Pictures. While filming certain scenes—especially those with a crowd of extras—the 30-year-old actor felt “incredibly nervous,” she said.

How did she manage to keep the situation under control? Thank her husband, Tom Holland, whom Zendaya says went to set that day to cheer her up. Spider-Man: Brand New Day star Holland also appears in The Odyssey as Telemachus, son of Odysseus and Penelope. And although he wasn’t scheduled to work at that particular moment, he showed up anyway to support his wife.

“I felt overwhelmed, to say the least,” Zendaya said at the screening, as reported by the Daily Mail, with the actor looking stunning in her cream-colored one-shoulder dress, pixie cut, and Christian Louboutin stilettos. “It was interesting because I was on a night shoot, and I remember I came in and I was like, This is like, a pinch-me moment…. I’m in front of these people who I’ve admired, but I’m just like, I don’t want to mess this up.”

While she admitted that these emotions might have worked for her character, they were not so good for her state of mind: “I was incredibly nervous, which I guess is helpful for the scene, but there’s so many other background actors as well who are performing their hearts out—so many—stunt performers who are performing and giving the most beautiful performances.”

The turning point came when Holland stepped behind the scenes to encourage her. “It helped that Tom came to set that day, and he was, like, in the corner like, ‘You got this, you’re doing good.’” It was a team effort.

Zendaya and Holland are one of Hollywood’s most admired couples, not only for their discretion (they quietly married last August 4 in Surrey) but also for the care with which they address sensitive issues, such as mental health. Even in the cult series Euphoria, Zendaya’s character, Rue, grapples with psychological issues—in addition to addiction—as a way to raise public awareness and combat the stigma that often surrounds these kinds of situations.
Originally published in Vanity Fair Italia.

items.title: Billy Crystal Answers the Proust Questionnaire
items.description: What is your idea of perfect happiness?
items.author: BILLY CRYSTAL
paragraphs: What is your idea of perfect happiness?
120/80 and a steady stream.
What is your greatest fear?
How this is all going to end.
Which historical figure do you most identify with?
Which living person do you most admire?
My wife, Janice. Fearless, smart, optimistic, hilarious, loving…adored by all.
What is the trait you most deplore in yourself?
Self-doubt. Wait, now I’m not sure of the answer. Was that okay? Can we come back to that one?
What is the trait you most deplore in others?
What is your greatest extravagance?
My imagination. And I like clothes.
What is your favorite journey?
From my dressing room to backstage—standing alone in the dark, a deep breath, and then feeling it’s time and walking out into the light.
What do you consider the most overrated virtue?
On what occasion do you lie?
When there’s a gun pointed at me.
What do you dislike most about your appearance?
Which living person do you most despise?
I’d rather not say, and thank you for your attention to this matter!
Which words or phrases do you most overuse?
“Sorry, I didn’t see your text till now.”
What is your greatest regret?
That my father died when I was 15 and never got to see my family, my career, and the man I think I am.
What or who is the greatest love of your life?
When and where were you happiest?
In the hospital waiting room, when my girls were born, and the doctor said everyone was fine.
Which talent would you most like to have?
What is your current state of mind?
If you could change one thing about yourself, what would it be?
I’d stop worrying about everyone all the time.
If you could change one thing about your family, what would it be?
That they’d finally understand why I worry about everyone all the time
What do you consider your greatest achievement?
We raised two fantastic daughters who became good, hard-working, honest people and great spouses and mothers in the middle of this business.
If you were to die and come back as a person or thing, what do you think it would be?
A New York Yankee with a sense of humor.
If you could choose what to come back as, what would it be?
What is your most treasured possession?
I lost them all, so I’d have to say my memory.
What do you regard as the lowest depth of misery?
Where would you like to live?
In the beautiful state of clarity.
What is your favorite occupation?
What is your most marked characteristic?
Determination, focus, self-starting.
What do you most value in your friends?
Love, empathy, loyalty, a sense of humor, and a handful of quarters for the parking meters.
Who are your favorite writers?
Hemingway, David Sedaris, Neil Simon, Herb Gardner, Arthur Miller, Victor Hugo.
Who is your favorite hero of fiction?
Santiago, the fisherman in The Old Man and the Sea.
Who are your heroes in real life?

Picasso, Muhammad Ali, Mickey Mantle, Buster Keaton, Sid Caesar, Mel Brooks, JFK, Alan Shepard—and Jim Redmond, a father who ran out of the stands at the ’92 Olympics to help his son, Derek, who had torn a hamstring in his race and was struggling to stand up and continue. They held onto each other and crossed the finish line together. Perfect.
What are your favorite names?
What is it that you most dislike?
A port-a-potty on a hot day.
How would you like to die?
Holding Janice’s hand. Ready, not frightened, satisfied, and with a smile and a goodbye to my family. And if there’s a laugh, that’s the last thing I hear? That would be great.

items.title: John Summit Is Extremely Mad Online About the Grammys
items.description: Every year, countless artists have their hopes and dreams dashed when the Recording Academy reveals its nominees for the Grammy Awards. For the most part, the unfortunately snubbed choose to lick their wounds in private. Maybe they toss out an oblique or pithy
items.author: Jon Blistein
paragraphs: Every year, countless artists have their hopes and dreams dashed when the Recording Academy reveals its nominees for the Grammy Awards. For the most part, the unfortunately snubbed choose to lick their wounds in private. Maybe they toss out an oblique or pithy quip on social media. Or maybe they make a video like Muna’s Katie Gavin, who copped to feeling disappointed, discussed the challenges of trying to shoehorn the band’s music into the Grammys’ sometimes overly-rigid genre categories, and still celebrated the artists who did get nominated.
But few show the chutzpah of DJ-producer John Summit, who took to X to proclaim, “Never submitting to the Grammys again unless shit changes, it’s all a fucking joke.”

Summit — who dropped his second album, Ctrl Escape earlier this year and was recently seen performing on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (cool) — was specifically frustrated with how the dance and electronic music categories shook out. “The whole dance category is just music industry fueled pop stars,” he lamented, insisting that the choices showed “zero respect for real electronic music & dj’s.” (And, he swore, “i’m not just talking about myself.”)

It is true that that the dance and EDM categories didn’t really feature any top-line DJs/producers besides Fred Again and Skrillex. And the categories were otherwise dominated by artists like Madonna, Robyn, Tinashe, Slayyyter, and Zara Larsson, who do present, at least on first glance, as pop musicians. But Summit went so far as to claim that these acts are “just not dance music, they’re pop,” and that “no DJ is playing that music in the clubs.”

Essays — perhaps even dissertations — could be written about how a person, let alone a professional DJ and producer, comes to think that, somehow, Madonna and Robyn do not make dance music. And that’s before you start to wonder if there’s maybe something telling about Summit’s focus on “pop stars,” “pop,” and the “lil teeny bopper pop stan accounts” flooding his replies, when noted psych rock band Tame Impala also got nominated in several dance and electronic music categories.

On top of all that, Summit’s tweets also manage to erase all the work put into this music by producers just like him. Nightfeelings, who worked on Tinashe’s Grammy-nominated “Melatonin,” astutely pointed this out to Summit, writing, “I actually come from dance music, my first project released on the same labels as aphex twin … I’ve performed at Berghain .. Andy weatherall played my tune Cheaters in every set for a while, I made a song with Romanthony .. just gonna leave it there.”
He then added, “Not to mention Tinashe is literally a dj.”

In vintage “im not mad. please dont put in the newspaper that i got mad” fashion, Summit ended his little polemic by trying to laugh off the whole thing. “Oh no i’m getting attacked hard on here. time to log off and continue my sold out arena tour for my real fans :)”

Not being able to help himself, he later hopped back on to pen, “i realized i didn’t do a good job of making my point earlier. my intent was not to drag other artists down and i seriously congratulate everyone who was nominated they fully deserve the recognition. i just think there should be an extra category for more dance music djs & producers much love everyone.” Summit then promised, signing off from twitter now for a while.”
Sure, man, whatever. Or, as Charli XCX put it, “not this guy again!”

items.title: Trump Lashes Out at 'Loser' Reporter for Questioning D.C. Renovation Obsession
items.description: A defensive Donald Trump lashed out at a reporter who asked him to justify why he was spending so much time renovating Washington, D.C., as opposed to more pressing issues like the aging air traffic control system, which glitched on Friday, abruptly halting ai
items.author: Tessa Stuart; Jack Crosbie
paragraphs: A defensive Donald Trump lashed out at a reporter who asked him to justify why he was spending so much time renovating Washington, D.C., as opposed to more pressing issues like the aging air traffic control system, which glitched on Friday, abruptly halting air travel across the country for the longest period since the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001.
“What do you say to critics who say you were too focused on D.C. construction projects while our airline systems were crumbling?” Trump was asked outside the White House on Monday.
“If you take a look at the White House, it’s flawless,” Trump replied.

But the question clearly touched a nerve because the president continued: “Listen to me, I know you don’t see dirt. But if you take a look at the White House — you’d never notice broken windows obviously from where you come.” Trump was speaking to NBC White House Correspondent Yamiche Alcindor, who is of Haitian descent.
Trump went on to declare, “The helipad has gotten great reviews,” while ignoring Alcindor’s follow-up questions about the weekend disruptions at airports across the U.S.

“Oh, you’re so pathetic,” Trump said as Alcindor pressed him about whether he and the Republican Party should have taken responsibility for not securing adequate funding to pay for upgrades to the air traffic control system. “I have a responsibility to make sure the symbol of our country is in decent shape — and it takes me 10 minutes a day. Very little time.”

“This doesn’t cost money. This is peanuts. This is called talent. Talent. You don’t have talent,” Trump said, continuing to insult the reporter. “The White House was in terrible condition, now it’s in beautiful condition. Cost me very little money to do it very little time to do and losers like you come out and say ‘Why are you focused on the White House?’”

Trump’s quest to reshape D.C. in his ideal image has resulted in an endless string of headlines and legal cases. The president has attempted to blast through red tape in order to accomplish his goals or get work done, upsetting the delicate balance of federal agencies and courts that govern who does what on public lands in D.C.

Most recently, Trump’s plans to build a triumphal arch came to a temporary halt when an irate federal judge claimed that the government’s lawyers had basically made up claims that the project would have some kind of benefit to the president’s physical security. Trump had previously mentioned he wanted to station snipers on the arch. His plan to revitalize the East Potomac Links golf course, as well, was halted by a court injunction when Trump’s legal team tried to pull a rush job with little notice, cutting down hundreds of trees in a single day. Trump has ranted online about the golf course several times in recent days, including posting several images depicting it in apparent despair. On Monday, he described the course as “Trash Island” while attacking the judge who ruled against his plans to renovate it.

Trump has always had a contentious relationship with the press, but has been making himself both more available and less agreeable to reporters in recent weeks. In September, he took the extraordinary step of outright banning several news outlets from the White House, yet continued to appear for interviews with the remaining press corps. In early October, likely feeling the stress of negative polls before the midterms, he blew up at reporters in the Oval Office for not asking him positive questions. He had a similar outburst later in the month.

The president is particularly sensitive to questions about his redecoration of the White House. During the waning days of the 2026 midterm campaign, former President Barack Obama joked that Trump’s renovations made the presidential home look like “Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” Trump lashed out in response, alleging that Obama couldn’t understand the imperative to beautify the White House because, like Alcindor, he doesn’t “notice dirt.”

items.title: Shakira Goes Global, Drake Gets Love, and More Latin Music Takeaways from the 2027 Grammy Nominations
items.description: The Recording Academy doesn’t always get it right when it comes to Latin music, but lately they’ve been trying. Last year, voters from the Latin Recording Academy were able to cast ballots in the standard edition, making for a more diverse voting pool. It’s a
items.author: Maya Georgi
paragraphs: The Recording Academy doesn’t always get it right when it comes to Latin music, but lately they’ve been trying. Last year, voters from the Latin Recording Academy were able to cast ballots in the standard edition, making for a more diverse voting pool. It’s a move that’s already paid off. Earlier this year, at the 2026 awards, Bad Bunny made history with the first Album of the Year win for a full Spanish-language album. Now, with the 2027 Grammy nominations, one of the biggest genres in the U.S. is still front and center — even if some of the nods are perplexing. Let’s take a look at all of the Latin music highlights from this year’s nominations.
Will Rosalía Follow in Bad Bunny’s Footsteps?

Rosalía just made history at the Latin Grammys when she became the first woman to win Album of the Year three times. Now, the Spanish singer is the second-most-decorated nominee for the 2027 Grammys, and she could follow Bad Bunny’s lead with another historic AOTY win. If Rosalía’s Lux snags the highest honor of the night, she would become the first woman to win in the category with a Spanish-language project.
Latin Music Newcomers Become First-Time Nominees

There were a handful of Latin music first-time nominees across categories. Ryan Castro secured two nods in the Best Música Urbana Album, one for his solo LP Hopi Sendé and another for his collaborative album with J Balvin, Omerta. Meanwhile, Argentine musician Milo J earned recognition in the Best Latin Song and Best Latin Rock or Alternative Album categories for his Latin Grammy-winning project La vida era Más Corta. Venezuelan American singer Elena Rose also received her first-ever Grammy nod, in the Best Latin Pop Album category. About that…
The Best Latin Pop Album Category Is a Mess

… Rose’s nomination leads us to the unfortunate catch-all that the Best Latin Pop Album category became this year. As we said, the Academy doesn’t always get it right when it comes to Latin music. Nowhere is that more blatant than this category, which is jam-packed with an array of popular Latin artists who make distinct music from each other. Karol G’s alternative album No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto makes some sense here, as does Mon Laferte’s Femme Fatale — but Carín León’s Muda runs the gamut of genres from norteño to salsa and soul. It makes no sense here, and Rawayana’s and Elena Rose’s genre-bending albums don’t really, either. Rather than find a way to honor these impressive works and the widely varied Latin genres they’re pushing forward, the Academy seems to be stuffing them under one confusing umbrella.
Drake Gets Recognition for Best Latin Song

Drake is up for Best Latin Song. Yes, you read that right: The rap superstar has received a nod for his Spanish-language feature on Karol G’s “Ahí.” It’s surprising in many ways, but especially considering Drake’s longstanding differences with the Academy; the last time he won a Grammy for one of his own songs, in 2019, he gave a speech about how little the awards mean to him, and he’s chosen not to submit his own work since then. The fact that the Academy nominated “Ahí” rather than Karol’s Bruno Mars collaboration “Still” is also a bit of a head-scratcher. But now Champagne Papi will go up against acts like Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso, Rosalía, Milo J, and Jorge Drexler.
Edgar Barrera and Songwriter of the Year: Third Time’s the Charm?

One of Latin music’s most sought-after collaborators is being recognized by the Academy once more. Edgar Barrera nabbed a third consecutive nod for Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical. He’s up against a field that includes Amy Allen and Theron Thomas, both of whom previously beat him. But after working on some of the year’s biggest Latin music projects and writing for Gracie Abrams, could this finally be the year the Recording Academy honors Barrera’s songwriting power?

There’s no denying Latin music’s worldwide takeover — just look at what Shakira and Anitta are doing. Both stars submitted their music beyond the Latin music categories, and they were recognized for continuing to expand their reach. Anitta’s latest album, Equilibrivm, received a nod for Best Global Music Album, while Shakira’s World Cup hit “Dai Dai” was nominated for Best Global Music Performance.

items.title: Elizabeth Debicki Says ‘Tenet’ Co-Star Robert Pattinson Will Be the ‘Perfect’ James Bond: ‘I’m So Thrilled’
items.description: Elizabeth Debicki is weighing in on her “Tenet” co-star Robert Pattinson becoming the next James Bond.
items.author: Marc Malkin; Payton Turkeltaub
paragraphs: Elizabeth Debicki is weighing in on her “Tenet” co-star Robert Pattinson becoming the next James Bond.

“I’m so happy for Rob,” said Debicki at the Los Angeles premiere of “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.” When asked why Pattinson will make the perfect Bond, she responded: “He is an enigma himself. He’s beautiful, and he’s funny, and he’s smart… I think he’s perfect. I’m so thrilled.”
Debicki also added that “he’s evolved so much as an actor. He’s made really interesting choices. He’s really smart.”
Debicki and Pattinson co-starred in Christopher Nolan’s 2020 sci-fi action film “Tenet” alongside John David Washington, Dimple Kapadia, Michael Caine, and Kenneth Branagh.
Amazon MGM announced Monday morning that Pattinson landed the role of 007 in the upcoming Bond film being directed by Denis Villeneuve

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

Amy Pascal, who has produced the “Spider-Man” franchise and several 007 films, and David Heyman, behind the “Harry Potter” series, are producing the new Bond film, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing. Steven Knight is writing the screenplay.

“Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” Villeneuve said. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”

items.title: Robert Pattinson Is Officially James Bond: Meet the New 007 Actor
items.description: It’s Pattinson, Robert Pattinson.
items.author: Jack Dunn; Ellise Shafer
paragraphs: It’s Pattinson, Robert Pattinson.

The “Batman” and “Odyssey” star has officially been cast as the next James Bond, ending months of rabid speculation about which young actor Amazon MGM and director Denis Villeneuve would hand the keys to the Aston Martin.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

Added Villeneuve, who recently directed Pattinson in the upcoming “Dune: Part Three”: “Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”

Amy Pascal, a key architect of the “Spider-Man” franchise, and David Heyman, behind the “Harry Potter” series, are producing the new Bond film, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing. Steven Knight is writing the screenplay.

Pattinson picks up the 007 mantle after Daniel Craig’s five-movie run as the womanizing super spy, which began in 2006 with “Casino Royale.” Craig’s final turn was in 2021’s “No Time to Die,” which ends with Bond sacrificing himself to save the world from a secret global terrorist organization. “No Time to Die” was also the last film in the series released before longtime producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli sold creative control of the franchise to Amazon MGM for $20 million.

Predictions about who would be the next James Bond had taken over media and the industry in the last month, and a shortlist of British actors took turns as the presumed favorite. Jacob Elordi was pegged for the role in the earliest days of swirling rumors, but reports since surfaced that the “Euphoria” star didn’t even screen test for the part. Jack Lowden seemed like another safe bet. In early September, his “Slow Horses” co-star Gary Oldman claimed Bond was already picked and cheekily added that his “fingers are crossed” for Lowden. However, Lowden’s run at the character was largely overshadowed by Callum Turner, who seemed like a sure pick until news of Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult’s auditions was revealed. At that point, it became anyone’s guess who would come out on top until Pattinson was ultimately chosen. Other actors in the mix included Josh O’Connor, Tom Francis, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Harris Dickinson and even Harry Styles.

It’s not hard to see from Amazon MGM’s perspective why Pattinson was the obvious choice. He is, almost unquestionably, 2026’s most in-demand movie star and has the box office record to show for it. With help from Zendaya, Pattinson drove A24’s “The Drama,” an intimate yet squirmy original dramedy, to $134 million worldwide from a budget of $28 million. “Primetime,” in which Pattinson starred as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen, likewise hit big with $61 million globally against a slim $18 million budget. Pattinson also starred as the sniveling Antinous in “The Odyssey,” which did $1.8 billion, and is set to star in “Dune: Part Three” in December, which is sure to pull in the big bucks. (It’s very possible Pattinson earned the part after impressing Villeneuve on Arrakis).

Pattinson also has the big IP experience needed to lead a franchise like James Bond. In 2022, Pattinson debuted as the titular Caped Crusader in Matt Reeves’ “The Batman.” He is set to revisit Gotham for the sequel in 2028. Those doubting Pattinson would land 007 often pointed to his obligations to Bruce Wayne as a reason why he could never take on Bond. However, after several production delays with “The Batman Part II,” it seems Pattinson is ready for a new longterm relationship with another familiar big-screen icon.

“James Bond is one of the most beloved, inspiring, iconic and yet enigmatic characters in literature and movies,” said producers Pascal and Heyman. “The legacy of this character is in great hands with Robert Pattinson. His fearlessness as an actor, his self-deprecating wit and his ability to continually reinvent himself make him the perfect Bond for our times.”

items.title: Brad Pitt Says ‘Ocean’s 14’ Not Shooting Until ‘Late’ 2027
items.description: Brad Pitt is giving an update on the shooting schedule of the much-anticipated “Ocean’s 14.”
items.author: Marc Malkin
paragraphs: Brad Pitt is giving an update on the shooting schedule of the much-anticipated “Ocean’s 14.”
“We’re talking about sometime late next year,” he told me Monday at the premiere of “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” in Hollywood.
The fifth installment of the “Ocean’s” franchise was supposed to start shooting next month after being postponed from June.
Clooney, Pitt, Julia Roberts, Matt Damon and Don Cheadle are set to reprise their roles. David Leitch is set to direct. “I tell you, Grant and George, they can write a good script,” Pitt said.

Clooney first teased there was a “great” script for “Ocean’s 14” in 2023. Roberts said at the Golden Globes in January, “Yes, I have seen a script. And I was kind of surprised, because I was like, ‘Oh, what is the story going to be?’ And it’s good. I mean, we wouldn’t do it if it’s not good.”

“The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is a sequel to Quentin Tarantino’s “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.” Quentin Tarantino wrote the script for the follow-up but handed the directing reins to David Fincher.

“The thing was dead on the shelf for like nine months,” Pitt said. “It goes that way a lot. Then one moment I had this idea … I gave it to [Fincher] when we got on a plane, we landed, and he said, ‘Yeah, I can do that.’ I called Quentin. He was into it, and here we are.”
Pitt won an Oscar for his work in the first movie: “I did have a little moment going, ‘Shit, what did I do in the first one?’ But you get right back into it.”

In the sequel, set a few years after the first in 1970s Los Angeles, Cliff has left Hollywood stunt work to become a projectionist at a movie theater in West Hollywood. He’s also an occasional hit man. Elizabeth Debicki plays his love interest, the talent agent of a television star (Scott Caan) who enlists Cliff’s help when he runs into trouble in the Philippines.
Pitt and Fincher first worked together 32 years ago making “Seven” in 1994. “It’s embarrassing how fortunate we are,” Pitt said. “It’s gross. Those two together are like hydrogen fusion.”
Pitt also said he is eager to do a sequel to his hit racing film “F1: The Movie.”

items.title: Grammy Nominations 2027: Raye Leads With 11 Noms as Rosalía, Olivia Rodrigo, Ella Langley and Other Female Artists Dominate
items.description: The full lineup of nominations for the 2027 Grammys was announced Monday morning, and most of the top artists that had been predicted to score big came through with impressive tallies. But one piece of the puzzle definitely did not go as foreseen — that it wou
items.author: Chris Willman
paragraphs: The full lineup of nominations for the 2027 Grammys was announced Monday morning, and most of the top artists that had been predicted to score big came through with impressive tallies. But one piece of the puzzle definitely did not go as foreseen — that it would end up being Raye leading the pack, and just how big her haul would be.

Raye leads all nominees with a startling 11 nods, followed by Rosalía with nine. Tied for seven nominations each are Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers. Following close behind with six nods each are Bruno Mars, Leon Thomas and Olivia Dean.

It’s not necessarily a fresh angle to point out that the Grammys have been favoring female artists as of late, but the disparity in gender representation has never been as dramatic as it is this year. In the category of album of the year, which many consider the Grammys’ most prestigious award, the eight nominations boil down to seven women and just one man (Bruno Mars being the lucky exception in that bunch). The same seven-to-one split goes for song of the year. For record of the year, six of the eight nominations go to women artists, and even then, one of the other two is for a male group with a woman as the featured artist (Tame Impala featuring Jennie).

The album of the year category will see Raye’s “This Music May Contain Hope” and a deluxe edition of Rosalía’s “Lux” face off against Bridgers’ “Lost Weekend,” Dean’s “The Art of Loving,” Langley’s “Dandelion,” Mars’ “The Romantic,” Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” and Swift’s “The Life of a Showgirl.”

With her nod for “The Life of a Showgirl,” Swift has tied the record for the artist to have the most consecutive albums nominated for record of the year: five. Only Kendrick Lamar joins her in having had that many new albums in a row compete for the big prize.

This year, Swift claimed a total of five nominations, including entries in the top three categories — album, record and song of the year — plus pop duo/group performance and song written for a motion picture. She split her submissions for record and song, choosing “The Fate of Ophelia” for her entry in the former category and the Disney song “I Knew It, I Knew You” for the latter division, and that paid off with nominations for both. “I Knew It, I Knew You” is, of course, the song that’s up as a movie theme song, and the title track of “The Life of a Showgirl,” a duet with Sabrina Carpenter, made it into the duo/group division.

Mars also took a similar approach to Swift in submitting different songs for record and song of the year, and it also paid off for him, as his album’s biggest hit, “I Just Might,” scored a chance at record, while arguably the most beloved track from his project, “Risk It All,” got the song of the year nom.

Otherwise, most top artists submitted the same tune for record and song of the year, as reflected in the final nominations. The numbers nominated for both include Dean’s “Man I Need,” Langley’s record-breaking “Choosin’ Texas,” Raye’s “Where Is My Husband!,” Rodrigo’s “The Cure,” and Rosalía’s “Berghain.”

Only two artists managed to score a nod in either record of the year or song of the year but not both. Tame Impala and Jennie’s “Dracula” is up for record but not song, and conversely, Ariana Grande’s “Hate That I Made You Love Me” made it in for song but not record.

The eight nominees for best new artist include Langley, who has a rare shot at sweeping all four top general categories this year. The others are Angine de Poitrine, Geese, Slayyyter, Sienna Spiro and Don Toliver.
Hip-hop did not have a banner year as far as the Grammys are concerned, with Toliver’s best new artist nomination being the only representation for that genre in any of the top general categories.

Others having a less stellar Grammy year than predicted include Harry Styles, who was completely shut out of the nominations. Noah Kahan also defied expectations by only picing up one nomination; although he had only been nominated for a Grammy twice before, he was predicted to have a bigger look this year with his blockbuster album and ticket sales and a degree of critical praise.

Plenty of other artists besides the aforementioned nominees managed to rack up multiple nominations. There is a large crop of 18 artists, producers or songwriters that managed to tie with an impressive four nods apiece, including some established Grammy favorites: Angine de Poitrine, Jon Batiste, Cardi B, Brandi Carlile, Doechii, Ariana Grande, Madonna, Jake Miller, PJ Morton, Kacey Musgraves, Zach Nahome, Daniel Nigro, David Rodriguez, Slayyyter, Tame Impala, Joybeth Taylor, Tems and Dylan Wiggins.

The list of people who came in just behind that with three nominations each is too long to mention, at 29 names — but it’s worth mentioning that one of those triple-nominees is Dolly Parton, who has three posthumous nominations. The late superstar was nominated in the best audiobook field, for the audio memoir “Star of the Show: My Life on Stage,” and she will also compete against herself with two nominations in the best country duo/group performance category.
The 69th annual Grammys will air Sunday, Feb. 7, 2027, at 4 p.m. PT/7 p.m. ET on ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu. The show will go out live from Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.
